prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Code · Config options with long tokens (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Option" · longest unbreakable word 131px · one-line width 131px
  col 2: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 334px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 537px · one-line width 537px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 501px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference/config-option table: readers look up one option by name and then check its default, see a realistic example value, and read what it does. It is scanned by row, not compared across rows, so row identity (the option key) must be findable instantly.","reading":"Vertical scan down column 1 to find the key, then a short rightward hop to Default/Example and finally the prose Description. Option and Default form the 'lookup' pair read together; Example and Description form the 'explanation' pair. Rows must read as units, so keys should not break and the long code tokens should not be shredded into unreadable fragments.","groups":["Option + Default: the identity/lookup pair, read together in one glance","Example + Description: the explanation pair, both wide and both needing generous width","Option alone must lead: it is the scan anchor and the only column whose values are all short, uniform identifiers"],"keep_intact":["Option keys (server.port, cache.ttlSeconds, auth.jwksUri) — the row's handle; 131px + 21px padding","Default values (8080, 300, —) — short, cheap to keep whole","The Example token is a single 537px unbreakable string: it can never be whole at 360px, so it must either be given a scrolling width or deliberately split"],"may_wrap":["Description — ordinary prose, wraps cleanly at any width and absorbs height","Default's rare long value (334px one-liner) can wrap rather than steal width from Option","Example may be split only if the design accepts scroll or a fragment; it should not be squeezed into a 60px sliver where it becomes noise"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [152, 111, 290, 190] · table 744×428px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 1 · OVERFLOWS the box by 384px
Design r1B: widths [152, 111, 360, 190] · table 814×428px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 1 · OVERFLOWS the box by 454px
Design r1C: widths [152, 111, 558, 190] · table 1012×428px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 652px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Option at 152 keeps every key whole (cache.ttlSeconds fits exactly), and Default at 111 keeps the code token %d{ISO8601} whole, so the lookup pair reads cleanly. Of the three it is the tightest table (744px) and the header row stays on one line.","problems":"The Description column is completely off-screen — the prose, which is the point of a config reference, is never seen. Meanwhile Example at 290px still shreds the URL into 'postgres://ap' / '.example.com...' (1 mid-word split), so those 290px buy no readable gain. Rows are uneven (36/60/106) because log.pattern's Default wraps to 4 lines inside a narrow cell, so the table reads as a stack of loose boxes rather than scannable rows.","cause":"Example 290 is far short of the 537px its token needs, so it splits anyway; and 152+111+290 already exceeds 360, pushing Description (190) past the viewport edge."},{"design":"r1B","good":"Giving Example 360 does show a slightly longer, more recognisable URL prefix, and the Option/Default pair is still intact and whole.","problems":"It pays 70px more than r1A for essentially the same readability: the token still breaks mid-word (1 split), because 360 < 537. Description is pushed even further out of reach, and the tall 106px rows and the 4-line Default wrap are unchanged. The extra width is pure scroll cost.","cause":"Example 360 is still under the 537px unbreakable width, so the split persists; the added 70px only worsens total overflow (814px)."},{"design":"r1C","good":"The only design that respects the content: Example at 558 holds the 537px token whole (0 mid-word splits), so the example values are readable as real code/URLs, and headers remain one line.","problems":"The table is 1012px — nearly three phone screens — and Description now sits 650px to the right, so the table degenerates into an example showcase with no explanation attached. The widest column is the one read least often, while the narrow prose column that carries the meaning is starved at 190. A reader scrolling to the URL loses the Option anchor entirely, breaking row identity.","cause":"Full 537px (+21) was granted to a token that appears in only a few rows, and Description was not compensated — the width budget is inverted relative to reading frequency."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"lean-scroll","widths":[152,111,140,170],"change":"Keep the locked lookup pair (Option 152 whole keys, Default 111 whole %d{ISO8601}) but stop paying for an unwrappable token: Example drops from 290–558 to 140 (still 2 readable URL lines, no worse than r1A's 290) and the saved ~150px goes to Description at 170 (149px of prose, ~4 lines). Total 573 — one and a half screens, so the prose is reachable in a single thumb-scroll instead of never."},{"name":"prose-first","widths":[152,111,115,205],"change":"Same insight, different weighting: Example is cut to the minimum that still shows a recognisable fragment (115 ≈ 2 short lines) and Description gets 205 (184px text, ~3 lines). This treats the table as a document to be read rather than a token gallery; total 583, the smallest total of the family that keeps all four columns functional."},{"name":"example-capped","widths":[152,111,230,180],"change":"A different bargain for readers who mainly want to copy the example: cap Example at 230 instead of r1C's 558. 230 shows roughly the first 80% of the postgres URL over two lines — visually almost as informative as 558 — while keeping Description only ~370px away (versus 650 in r1C), so the row's explanation is one short scroll from its key rather than lost in a three-screen table. Total 673."}]}
